title: The call in the ear
hookLine: a newborn's first sounds in this world, and a custom that makes them the call to prayer

lines: A WHISPER IN THE RIGHT EAR.
cards: A hospital room, minutes after a birth. Monitors beeping. Someone crying, someone laughing, someone already on the phone.
And in some Muslim families, a father or grandfather leans down close to the baby's right ear and, very softly, says: Allahu akbar. Allah is greater.
Then the rest of the call to prayer, whispered, to someone who has never heard a word. The first words, before the name, before anything else.

teach.b: First, the source. It isn't a verse of the Qur'an.
It's a report from Abu Rafi', who served the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.
In Sunan Abu Dawud and Jami' at-Tirmidhi, he says, in paraphrase: I saw the Messenger of Allah give the call to prayer in the ear of al-Hasan ibn 'Ali when Fatimah gave birth to him.

Al-Hasan was the Prophet's grandson, so the custom traces back to a grandfather leaning over a newborn. Second, the strength of the report. Tirmidhi graded it sound, and noted that people acted on it.
Some scholars have questioned its chain. So you'll find families who keep the custom carefully and others who don't, and both have reasons.
Some families also say the iqamah, the second call that begins a prayer, in the left ear, following other reports.

Third, the words: Allahu akbar; I bear witness there is no god but Allah; I bear witness Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; come to prayer; come to success. Said to a baby, it's not a summons to get up and pray.
It's more like a welcome: the first thing this person hears is the name of Allah and the shape of the life ahead. Fourth, a reflection some readers share.

teach.h: A LIFE BETWEEN CALL AND PRAYER.
teach.b: They note that the funeral prayer has no call before it, and say a life is lived between the two: the call whispered at birth, and the prayer said at the end. The time in between is how long it takes to answer.

how: In some Muslim families a parent or elder softly recites the adhan in a newborn's right ear soon after birth, and some also recite the iqamah in the left ear; others do not keep the custom.

recite a long surah over him.
wait silently until the seventh day.
games.why: Abu Rafi': I saw the Messenger of Allah give the call to prayer in the ear of al-Hasan when Fatimah gave birth to him.

practice: Think of a baby born recently, in your family, among friends, or one you only heard about; if no one comes to mind, think of all the babies being born somewhere during this breath.

Picture a small face, and the first sounds reaching that ear. If you pray, you can make du'a for that child by name, or for every child born today; if not, hold one wish for them: that the first words they hear be kind ones.

wordCard.voice: The call in the ear. The adhan whispered into a newborn's right ear, from the report of Abu Rafi' about al-Hasan, so the first words a child hears are Allahu akbar. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the call to prayer; in this custom, the first words a newborn hears.

carryVoice: Your line: the first words. Allah's name, before the name, before anything else. See you tomorrow.
